data.title: Nvidia declines, adding to evidence of an AI bubble destined to pop, says SA analyst
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) ended -2.9% on Wednesday despite reporting revenue and profits that exceeded analyst expectations, as Seeking Alpha analyst Daniel Jones warned that "evidence is continuing to grow that we are truly in an AI bubble that is destined to pop."

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended +0.4, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.1%.

Nvidia’s (NVDA) almost 30% decline over the past month is adding to worries within the technology space, Jones said.

In addition, the Federal Reserve released its October meeting minutes, with the central bank warning that artificial intelligence acts as "a driver of both inflation and potential financial instability.”.

The Fed also warned that future interest rate hikes would very likely occur.

Investors are assigning almost a 92% chance that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates by 25 basis points, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

While central bank reports project inflation could fall sharply in upcoming years, Jones noted this would likely come at a cost.

"I actually think that is likely to occur, though I expect it to be as part of the fallout involving a stagflationary recession," the analyst said.

data.title: Yelp announces workforce reduction affecting nearly 5% of employees
data.description:
• Yelp (YELP) announced a workforce reduction on November 18, 2026, expected to affect nearly 5% of its full-time employees.
  • The company plans to reinvest the substantial majority of resulting cost savings into its business, focusing on high-return growth opportunities, particularly AI-powered offerings.
  • Yelp expects restructuring charges of ~$14M–$16M, primarily in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.
  • The charges will include severance payments and related employee benefit costs and are expected to reduce net income but not adjusted EBITDA.
  • The company maintained its FY2026 revenue guidance of $1.455B–$1.460B.
  • FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance remains unchanged at $320M–$325M.
  • Yelp intends to exclude workforce reduction-related charges from its non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted EBITDA.

data.title: IM Cannabis to consolidate share for Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
• IM Cannabis (IMCC) said on Wednesday that its board has approved a 3:1 share consolidation of its issued and outstanding common shares, no par value per share.
  • The primary purpose of the consolidation is to increase the per-share trading price of the common shares to support the company's efforts to maintain compliance with Nasdaq's US$1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing, the company added. 
  • The company anticipates the common shares to begin trading on the Nasdaq on a post-consolidation basis at the opening of trading on November 23, 2026.
  • Following the consolidation, the issued and outstanding common shares are expected to be reduced from 1,844,162 to nearly 614,721 shares.
  • Press Release

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Thursday
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages finished mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. The Nasdaq ended higher even as Nvidia closed lower.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended +0.4, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.1%.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Thursday:

  • Take-Two Interactive's (TTWO) Grand Theft Auto 6 will be officially released about 13 years since GTA 5 hit the market. The highly-anticipated video game will be natively available on Sony's (SONY) PlayStation 5 and PS5 Pro, as well as Microsoft's (MSFT) Xbox Series X|S.
  • When Alibaba (BABA) reported second-quarter earnings before the opening bell, investors will be keenly watching for the firm’s AI- and cloud-related revenue and its capital expenditure. Earnings are expected to more than double this quarter to $1.65 per share, due to a weak last-year comparison. The top line is projected to see a 16% Y/Y jump to $40.49B.
  • Walmart (WMT) is also set to release its fiscal Q3 earnings results before market open, with Wall Street, on average, expecting the retail giant to post a quarterly EPS of $0.64 on revenue of $187.25B.

data.title: QuantumScape extends losses to seventh straight session
data.description:
QuantumScape (QS) widened its losing streak to the seventh straight session on Wednesday after registering steep declines in recent trading. The shares ended 2.74% lower at $3.19.

Between November 10 and November 17, shares of the lithium metal battery maker plunged more than 26% compared to a 2.4% fall in the broader markets.

On a year-to-date basis, QuantumScape has tumbled nearly 69% compared to a 7% rise in the S&P500 index.

In October, the company reported a narrower third-quarter loss of $0.14 per share. QuantumScape ended the quarter with $819.8M in liquidity and reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $250M to $275M and capital expenditure outlook of $27M to $37M.

As per Seeking Alpha’s quant rating, QS has a Hold rating with a score of 2.50 out of 5. The firm has been rated an F for profitability and momentum, while it has been graded a C for valuation.

Seeking Alpha analysts have assigned a Hold rating for QS with one Hold and one Sell call. Meanwhile, Wall Street analysts have seven Hold calls and 2 Strong Sell ratings for the stock. Overall, Wall Street analysts have issued a Hold call for the company.
